scope: Table 166 AP/AS and §12.5.5/Table 170 normal, rollover, down appearance selection; stored stream versus state subdictionary; producer AP presence versus reader fallback. No full annotation-subtype or appearance-geometry certification.

locators.appearance_algorithm_and_states: §12.5.5 begins physical p. 489 / printed p. 474; Table 170 and first state example are physical p. 490 / printed p. 475; state-selection and processor behavior continue physical p. 491 / printed p. 476

effective_rules: Table 166 AP is optional in the dictionary, but a PDF 2.0 writer shall include AP when writing/updating except when Rect has zero width AND zero height, or Subtype is Popup, Projection, or Link. EC3 #22 makes this version-specific rule explicit: PDF 1.2–1.7 retains optionality.

If AP is present, §12.5.5/Table 170 requires N; optional R and D default to N. N is used when idle and for printing; R is used on cursor-over without button press; D is used when pressed/held inside the active area.

Each N/R/D value may be one appearance stream or a dictionary of named state streams. Table 166 requires annotation AS if AP has one or more subdictionaries; the state example and §12.5.5 select by AS. When a present AS names no state, the reader shall attempt reasonable behavior, with displaying nothing as the explicit example.

A processor lacking native support for an annotation subtype shall render its N appearance. Absence of AP has implementation-dependent rendered appearance under EC3 #34; the producer AP rule must not be turned into a required reader rejection or one universal synthesized image.
